clue.text: Evangelist depressed by lower prices

parts.note: Mark is one of the four Gospel writers, the Evangelists
depressed means down, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A gospel writer feels gloomy about falling shop prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A markdown is a reduction in the price of goods, so lowering prices is the same idea.

clue.text: MP's constituent

definitions.meaning: an MP, short for ... of Parliament, is a ... of the House: the 's reads as is
a constituent is a component part, one element of a whole

explanation.surface: A voter in a parliamentary member's district.
explanation.definitionFit: A member is both an elected representative and one component part of a larger body.

clue.text: Artist going to bank once in a blue moon

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A painter visits the bank only very occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom; once in a blue moon is the idiom for something very infrequent.

clue.text: Alain's girl entered contest

indicators.note: entered means went into, so the girl goes inside the surname

parts.note: Alain Delon was a French film star, so his surname comes from Alain's
Cath is a girl's name, short for Catherine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's daughter took part in a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alain's' points to the French film star Alain Delon, whose surname is cut open by the girl's name; 'entered' signals that insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics competition of ten events, so a contest.

clue.text: Butterfly has a holiday, having captured the heart of Pinkerton, a naval officer

parts.note: Whit, short for Whitsun, is a church festival and holiday

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here from the nine letters of Pinkerton

parts.note: an admiral is a senior naval officer

explanation.surface: Madame Butterfly takes a break, having won over Pinkerton, the naval officer of the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Puccini's opera, where Butterfly loves the naval lieutenant Pinkerton. 'the heart of' gives E, the middle letter of PINKERTON; 'has' and 'having captured' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The white admiral is a woodland butterfly, black with white bands across its wings.

clue.text: Brand leader in trouble — there's a letter about it

indicators.note: about means going round, so the letter is placed around the other piece

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, taken here from trouble

explanation.surface: The head of a troubled brand gets a letter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SIGMA around T, the first letter of 'trouble'; 'it' in the surface points to that T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, a brand in the sense of a burnt-in mark of shame.

clue.text: Belgian port excluding an idiot

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Antwerp is a major port in Belgium

explanation.surface: A Belgian harbour city keeps out a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or foolish person, an idiot.

clue.text: Labour outcast initially seen in part of Ireland or part of Scotland

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so these letters go within the place name

parts.note: Galway is a county and city in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A rejected Labour politician turns up in a region of Ireland or of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives L and O from 'Labour outcast'; 'seen in' puts them inside GALWAY. Galloway is a region of south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloway is a historic region in south-west Scotland, now part of Dumfries and Galloway.

clue.text: Prince Henry follows car, shaking fist

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the Henry letter is placed after the jumbled car
shaking means agitating, so the letters of car are jumbled

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
dukes is slang for fists, so a duke is a fist

explanation.surface: Royal Henry walks behind a vehicle, waving his fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' scrambles the three letters of the vehicle, and 'follows' puts Henry's symbol after them; 'put up your dukes' is old slang for raising your fists.
explanation.definitionFit: An archduke was a prince of the Austrian imperial house, so the title names a prince.

clue.text: Maniac or mad material

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters have gone wild and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lunatic or a crazy person is described, with some cloth tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges MANIAC and OR together into the fabric name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marocain is a crinkled dress fabric of silk or wool, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: United Nations entertaining the Spanish writer

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding a guest within

parts.note: a bloc is a group of nations united by a common interest
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: The UN plays host to a writer from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' signals that the group of nations hosts the Spanish article. Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French writer of verse and essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was a prolific writer, known for cautionary verses for children.

clue.text: Modify particles in rows

parts.note: to alter is to modify or change
cations are positively charged ions, a kind of particle

explanation.surface: Someone instructs us to rearrange particles in lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like lines, but rhyming with 'cows' it means quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Altercations are noisy arguments, and rows (rhyming with cows) are quarrels.

clue.text: Great success cooks celebrate without beer

indicators.note: cooks means fiddles or falsifies, so the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Chefs throw a party with no beer to mark a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' rearranges CELEBRATE; 'without' says the letters of BEER come out of that pool, leaving C, L, A, T, E to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, a dazzling achievement.

clue.text: Form solid pile in solid form

indicators.note: form means shape or fashion into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shapes a heap into a solid shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' at the start is the instruction to rearrange SOLID PILE; the 'form' at the end belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsoid is a three-dimensional shape whose cross-sections are ellipses, a solid geometric figure.

clue.text: At sea draw black and red seaweed

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Out on the ocean, someone sketches a black and red seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges DRAW, BLACK and RED; the 'and' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladderwrack is a common brown seaweed with air-filled bladders on its fronds.

clue.text: Questionable word from Juliet demanding hero with fewer flaws?

indicators.note: flaws means cracks or faults, which break up the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Juliet wants a hero with fewer faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaws' rearranges HERO and FEWER; 'with' and 'demanding' only join. Juliet asks 'wherefore art thou Romeo?', meaning why, not where, are you Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: Wherefore means why; Juliet's famous line uses it to ask a question, hence a questioning word.

clue.text: Paint food container

definitions.meaning: a paint finish with a slight sheen, between matt and gloss
the casing round an egg, which holds the food inside

explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell names both a low-sheen paint finish and the hard casing of an egg.

clue.text: Navigator held back by hiccups eventually

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sailor is delayed by a bout of hiccups that eventually passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' signals the letters are concealed in 'hiccups eventually'. Amerigo Vespucci was the Italian navigator after whom America is named.
explanation.definitionFit: Amerigo Vespucci was an Italian explorer and navigator whose voyages gave America its name.

clue.text: Ecofriendly fellow cautiously moves birds

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
to inch is to move slowly and carefully, so inches means cautiously moves

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded man edges warily towards some birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfinches are small green-and-yellow finches, so they are birds.

clue.text: Colour round head of Davy Jones

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the architect's first name goes about the other letter

parts.note: Inigo Jones was a famous English architect

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from Davy

explanation.surface: A tint around the leader of the fabled sea locker of the drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Davy Jones' suggests the sailor's devil of the deep, but it splits: the D of 'Davy' and Inigo for 'Jones', the architect; 'round' puts INIGO about D.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet colour, one of the seven colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Condition beginning to deteriorate, so it's said

parts.note: a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from deteriorate

explanation.surface: A situation starts to get worse, or so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or expressed in words, the same as said.

clue.text: I interrupt to oust petitioner

indicators.note: interrupt means break into, so I goes inside the other word

parts.note: to supplant someone is to oust or replace them

explanation.surface: Someone breaks in to throw out a person making a request.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant is someone who humbly begs or petitions for something.

clue.text: All of Israel oddly neglected French runner

indicators.note: neglecting the odd letters means only the even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: All of a Middle Eastern country oddly ignored a French athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first, third, fifth letters and so on of 'All of Israel' keeps L, O, I, R, E. 'Runner' is a crossword way of saying river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, and a river is a runner in crossword language.

clue.text: Artist in the modern style

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: An artist working in a contemporary manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters spans the end of 'modern' and the start of 'style'. Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a leading Dada and Surrealist painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Prompt about cover for maths book

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cue is a prompt, as given to an actor
a lid is a cover for a box or pot

explanation.surface: A prompt to find the cover for a mathematics textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CUE into EUC. Euclid's Elements was the standard geometry textbook for centuries, so 'Euclid' came to mean a geometry book.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid, the Greek mathematician, gave his name to his Elements, long used as the school geometry book.

clue.text: Driver with case of wet rot turned back

indicators.note: case of means the first word forms a casing round the second

parts.note: moist means wet or damp

indicators.note: turned back says the word rot is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A motorist whose car body is covered in damp rot that has been reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses the decay word, and 'case of' wraps the damp word around the result, so the surface's car-body image hides the construction.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a car, so a driver.

clue.text: US measure to besiege terrorist centre? Hang about!

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so the measure goes round the other piece

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a measure of volume

indicators.note: the centre of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter, taken from terrorist

explanation.surface: An American unit surrounds the core of a terror cell, and someone shouts to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' gives O, the middle letter of 'terrorist'; 'to besiege' puts LITER around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about or linger idly; the exclamation reads as an imperative.

clue.text: Heavenly body of retrospective designer — and French sex appeal

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous French fashion designer
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A retrospective exhibition of a couturier, with some Gallic allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' turns the whole run DIOR-ET-SA backwards, giving AS-TE-ROID.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, so a heavenly body.
